name: f-microwave
style: You are a seasoned documentary narrator telling a surprising true story from history in a short video. Warm, curious, grounded, quietly amazed. Natural unhurried pace. Slow down on every year and number and let it land. Small pause before a reveal. The very last line is unfinished: keep the voice lifted and suspended, as if the sentence continues, never a falling final tone. Never rushed, never shouty, never robotic.

lines.text: In nineteen forty-five, a chocolate bar melted in an engineer's pocket.
Nobody had turned on a stove.
Percy Spencer was testing magnetrons, the tubes that powered wartime radar.
He guessed the invisible waves had cooked his snack.
So he held popcorn kernels up to the tube.
They popped all over the lab.
His company built the first microwave oven in nineteen forty-seven.
It stood almost six feet tall and weighed about seven hundred fifty pounds.
It went to restaurants and ships, not homes.
Twenty years later, a countertop model hit stores for four hundred ninety-five dollars.
Today, more than nine in ten American homes have one.
The waves make the water in food spin back and forth, and that motion becomes heat.
